name: poster
description: A framed print for the wall, new each day: Bauhaus, Swiss, Constructivist, ridgeline, Memphis and sunburst posters drawn from a seed, public-domain museum prints, or AI posters with the words set in real type.

settings.name: fal_api_key
settings.label: fal.ai API key (AI posters)
settings.help: Only the AI styles need one, at about US$0.04 a poster with Nano Banana or US$0.01 with FLUX Schnell. Each subject is painted once per style and shape, then kept. Leave empty to use the key under Settings › Generative AI. Get one at https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys.

settings.name: gen_daily_usd
settings.label: AI budget per day
settings.help: The most the AI styles may spend in a day. One poster a day is about US$0.04. 0 is no limit.

settings.name: gen_per_refresh
settings.label: New AI posters started per preview
settings.help: How many new pictures one settled preview in the editor may start (1 to 50).

settings.name: gen_parallel
settings.label: AI posters made at once
settings.help: How many pictures fal.ai works on side by side (1 to 8).

choices.label: Woodblock: ink print with a Japanese label (AI)
Travel poster: screen print with a place name (AI)
Linocut: black ink and one colour (AI)
Mix: a different free style each time

cell_options.name: change
cell_options.label: New poster
cell_options.help: How often the poster changes. An AI style paints each new subject once, so hourly with a long list costs the most.

cell_options.name: title
cell_options.label: Title (drawn styles)
cell_options.help: The headline on a drawn poster. {weekday}, {day}, {month}, {monthnum} and {year} become to-day's. Empty uses the style's own, mostly the weekday.

cell_options.name: subtitle
cell_options.label: Second line (drawn styles)
cell_options.help: The small line under the title, with the same placeholders. Empty uses the date.

cell_options.name: subjects
cell_options.label: Subjects (AI styles)
cell_options.help: One a line, taken in turn: subject | label | year. For example: Aireys Inlet | Split Point | 1891, or Laughing kookaburra | ワライカワセミ. The subject is looked up on Wikipedia for the small print. Empty uses the style's own list of birds, places, parks or plants.

cell_options.name: facts
cell_options.label: Small print from Wikipedia
cell_options.help: The opening sentences of the subject's Wikipedia article on the travel, linocut and botanical posters.

cell_options.name: museum_query
cell_options.label: Museum search (gallery styles)
cell_options.help: Your own search of the Art Institute of Chicago's public-domain works, such as Hokusai, Mondrian or still life. Empty walks the style's own list of artists.
